name: hss.db
tagline: Commercial embedded object database for .NET and Xamarin with a LINQ query engine (c. 2009–2017).
description: hss.db was an embedded object-relational database for .NET from HighSpeed-Solutions LLC. Written entirely in C#, mostly as a portable class library with thin per-platform adapters, it stored .NET objects with optional predefined schemas, binary serialization and encryption, and queried them through an IQueryable LINQ provider, with ACID transactions and zero configuration. Version 4.0, published on NuGet in March 2016, targeted .NET 4.6, Xamarin Android and iOS, Windows Phone 8.1 and Windows 10 UWP, and a LINQPad driver was available. It was sold commercially. The vendor's site went dark around 2017 and no newer packages exist; LiteDB, Realm or SQLite with an ORM cover the same ground today.
statusNote: No packages since 4.0.0 (March 2016) and the vendor site has been offline since about 2017. Consider LiteDB or SQLite.

pricing.notes: Sold through a Buy Now page on the vendor site; terms and prices are no longer available.

strengths: Full IQueryable LINQ provider over embedded objects
Single C# codebase across desktop, UWP and Xamarin mobile
Encryption and ACID transactions with zero configuration
weaknesses: Vendor gone; no updates or support
Closed source and tied to 2016-era .NET targets
useCases: Maintaining legacy Xamarin or UWP apps built on it
Planning a migration of such apps to LiteDB or SQLite
